chk_problem.label: accurate
chk_problem.poster_evidence: Roof construction, maintenance, installation, and inspection expose workers to significant slipping and falling risks. Many roof tasks are also physically demanding and repetitive, providing strong motivation for robotic assistance.
chk_problem.reason: The poster accurately describes the research problem as investigating the feasibility of using quadruped robots for hazardous and repetitive roof tasks, matching the paper's description.

chk_method.label: accurate
chk_method.poster_evidence: An adjustable tiled-roof test rig was developed using Frankfurter Pfanne tiles, the most common roof tile type in Germany. A Unitree Go2 running software version 1.4.4 was evaluated in three core skills: balancing on increasing inclines, performing get-up and lie-down sequences, and walking uphill.
chk_method.reason: The poster describes the method of using a roof test rig and evaluating the Unitree Go2 robot's performance, consistent with the paper.

chk_data.label: accurate
chk_data.poster_evidence: An OptiTrack motion-capture system tracked reflective markers attached to the sides of the front-left and rear-left feet. Slippage was defined as cumulative foot displacement opposing the walking direction while vertical displacement remained below 1.0 mm, thereby excluding swing-phase motion.
chk_data.reason: The poster mentions the use of Frankfurter Pfanne tiles and the OptiTrack motion capture system, aligning with both drafts of the paper's description of the dataset.

chk_setup.label: accurate
chk_setup.poster_evidence: An adjustable tiled-roof test rig was developed using Frankfurter Pfanne tiles, the most common roof tile type in Germany. A Unitree Go2 running software version 1.4.4 was evaluated in three core skills: balancing on increasing inclines, performing get-up and lie-down sequences, and walking uphill. Each experiment was repeated ten times.
chk_setup.reason: The poster describes the experimental setup, including the test rig, tiles, OptiTrack system, and controlled trials, consistent with both drafts of the paper's description.

chk_primary_result.label: accurate
chk_primary_result.poster_evidence: Walking trials covered inclines from 0° to 25°. The practical maximum walking incline was 20°, while frequent falls occurred at 25°. Slippage increased quadratically with inclination, while measured friction coefficients suggested much higher theoretical limits.
chk_primary_result.reason: The poster states the primary result of slippage increasing quadratically and critical failures occurring at 25°, consistent with both drafts of the paper's description.

chk_secondary_result.label: accurate
chk_secondary_result.poster_evidence: The critical angle for balanced standing was 27.58° ± 0.72°. Failure was primarily caused by automatic limb repositioning following foot slippage or atypical joint configurations. Get-up and lie-down motions succeeded only up to 11° in head-up and head-down orientations and 7° sideways.
chk_secondary_result.reason: The poster includes the critical angle for standing and the limitations of get-up/lie-down sequences, consistent with one of the paper's drafts for secondary results.

chk_baseline.label: accurate
chk_baseline.poster_evidence: Without significant modification, the Unitree Go2 was not suited for operation in roof environments. The measured friction coefficient was 1.144 ± 0.1299 on flat tile sections and 1.430 ± 0.1298 on curved sections.
chk_baseline.reason: The poster describes the baseline performance of the Unitree Go2 robot on the roof test rig with standard ball feet, consistent with one of the paper's drafts.

chk_conclusion.label: accurate
chk_conclusion.poster_evidence: An unmodified Unitree Go2 failed before reaching many common residential roof inclines. Balanced standing became critical at 27.58° ± 0.72°, get-up and lie-down motions were limited to 7°–11°, and frequent walking failures occurred at 25°. Slippage increased quadratically with inclination, while measured friction coefficients suggested much higher theoretical limits. This gap demonstrates that dynamic stability, terrain interactions, and incline-aware control are as important as material friction.
chk_conclusion.reason: The poster accurately concludes that unmodified quadrupeds are not capable of safe and reliable operation in roof environments, matching the paper's conclusion.

chk_limitation.label: accurate
chk_limitation.poster_evidence: Further studies should compare multiple quadruped platforms, gaits, and walking speeds. Tests should also include payloads, debris, vegetation, moisture, weather, and changing surface conditions. These factors are expected to reduce performance and increase uncertainty beyond the ideal conditions evaluated here.
chk_limitation.reason: The poster mentions the limitation that experiments were conducted under ideal conditions without external factors, consistent with the paper.
